correctness.rationale: The support bound proves three rounds necessary for all initial vectors. Full support after three rounds is equivalent to an all-ones unnormalized product: each of eight initial entries appears exactly once with coefficient 1/8. Edge overlap gives a size-two intermediate support and excludes completion. Contracting the four first-matching edges yields exactly the two loopless degree-two multigraph types. Inclusion-exclusion counts 60 edge-disjoint matchings, 12 of two-cycle type and 48 of single-cycle type. Complements of four-element supports give respectively 24 and 4 possible completing third matchings. Hence 480/105^2=32/735. Exact integer matrix replay checks the entire conditional sample space and an independently chosen first matching. The proof is universal over every real initial vector; no finite experiment is used as a proof beyond the eight-vertex finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Inspected the defining 2019 block-gossip full text, the 2010 deterministic finite-time-consensus thesis, the full 2011 finite-time stochastic-graph analysis, and the 2006 gossip paper. Each treats the averaging primitive, existence, or convergence estimates but none of their inspected theorems determines the exact probability 32/735 and conditional 24-versus-4 completion law for three iid uniform perfect matchings of eight labeled agents. Targeted semantic-index and web searches on aliases and matching-cycle classes found no same or stronger covering claim. Index coverage is incomplete and a specialized earlier enumeration remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: Eight nodes form the first power-of-two synchronous binary-averaging instance whose edge-disjoint second matching can have two different alternating-cycle topologies. The exact probability of minimum-round universal consensus is a natural reliability invariant for random parallel gossip. The two structural cases yield a sharp sixfold difference in their final-round completion chance, a nontrivial scheduling insight distinct from approximate consensus rates or mere deterministic reachability. Exact full classification is useful without claiming a higher-dimensional algorithm or runtime improvement.
